extracted.intended_audience: ACUS members, consultants, agency officials, and other stakeholders involved in producing or using ACUS recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance describing how the Administrative Conference of the United States develops, approves, and implements Recommendations (and occasional Statements), including roles for the Office of the Chairman, consultants, committees, the Council, and the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory function — convene public and private sectors to recommend improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should arise from ACUS’s statutory role of convening diverse stakeholders (public and private) with the goal of improving administrative and regulatory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement of consultants with Council approval
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of the Council, engages consultants to study administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before initiating a study, the Office of the Chairman must obtain Council approval to engage external consultants (or rely on in-house staff) to examine targeted administrative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive research report proposing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants or in-house staff then prepare a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies should result in a comprehensive research report that articulates proposed recommendations based on the investigation; the report is the substantive foundation for subsequent committee and Council consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discussion and drafting of Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACUS committee discusses this report, preparing a draft Recommendation to submit to the Council and, with approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A committee must review the research report, deliberate on its findings, and produce a draft Recommendation intended for Council review; committee work translates research into formal draft text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council review and approval to transmit to Assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft Recommendation is submitted to the Council and, with the Council’s approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council serves as an intermediate approval body; only Council-approved drafts are forwarded to the Assembly for final consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly debate and adoption of final Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a debate the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation, which ACUS undertakes to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assembly debates the Council‑approved draft and, upon adoption, the Recommendation becomes ACUS policy/position and triggers implementation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation responsibility for adopted Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS undertakes to implement adopted Recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the Assembly adopts a Recommendation, ACUS is responsible for implementing it — implying follow-through and operational steps beyond mere adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Statements as non‑binding outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the ACUS membership has acted to adopt a “Statement” to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements are typically produced by the same process that leads to Recommendations but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments rather than formal recommendations; they are distinct from Recommendations and are cataloged alongside them in the database.
